name: Ajax 1994/95
description: Ajax, Champions League winners in 1995, with a young core, positional play and wingers attacking down the flanks.

name: Arsenal 2005–11
description: Wenger's Arsenal, with short passes and combinations through the middle, a young core and no trophies in the Emirates era.

name: Atlético Madrid 2013/14
description: Simeone's Atlético, Spanish champions with a compact block, direct counter-attacks and intense zonal marking.

name: Barcelona 2008–12
description: Guardiola's Barcelona: long possession, short passing, high pressing and a core of academy players.

name: Brazil 1982
description: Telê Santana's squad at the 1982 World Cup in Spain: talent, technique and futebol-arte, with freedom for the stars.

name: Borussia Dortmund 2010–13
description: Klopp's Dortmund: counter-pressing, quick transitions and physical intensity, twice German champions.

name: Flamengo 1980
description: Coutinho's Flamengo: a technical side with the ball on the ground and freedom for the stars, 1980 Brazilian champions.

name: Fluminense 2023
description: Diniz's Fluminense: possession with short passing, position rotation and its own identity, Copa Libertadores champions in 2023.

name: Grêmio 2017
description: Renato's Grêmio: possession that goes forward with purpose, play through the middle and a focus on results, Libertadores champions in 2017.

name: Inter 2009/10
description: Mourinho's Inter: direct counter-attacks, a mid-to-low block, zonal marking and the treble.

name: Juventus 2014–19
description: Allegri's Juventus: pragmatic and adaptable, with a mid-to-low block, a focus on results and a tradition of winning titles.

name: Leeds United 2019/20
description: Bielsa's Leeds: very high pressing, man-marking, vertical attacks down the wings and a system that does not change.

name: Liverpool 2021/22
description: Klopp's Liverpool: a 4-3-3 with high pressing, relational rotations and full-backs providing width, almost winning everything.

name: Mamelodi Sundowns 2025
description: Cardoso's Mamelodi Sundowns: possession with combinations through the middle, zonal defence and technical players, with the plan adapted to each opponent.

name: Manchester City 2017/18
description: Guardiola's Manchester City: positional play, high pressing, a 4-3-3 with wingers and a technical, athletic squad, English champions with 100 points.

name: Manchester United 1995/96
description: Ferguson's Manchester United: a 4-4-2 with quick wingers, a young core and the coach's authority, focused on results.

name: Milan 1988–91 (Sacchi)
description: Sacchi's Milan: collective high pressing, pure zonal marking, a system above the stars and an identity imposed by the coach.

name: Milan 2006/07
description: Ancelotti's Milan: a midfield diamond with Pirlo as the pivot, freedom for Kaká and the stars, a mid block and a focus on results.

name: Netherlands 1974
description: Michels' Oranje: high pressing, total football with fluid roles, possession and a coach with strong authority.

name: Vasco 2026 (Pedro Emanuel)
description: Pedro Emanuel's Vasco: pressing and possession that goes forward quickly, attacks down the wings and a focus on results, with the plan adapted to each opponent.

name: Wolves 1949–60
description: Stan Cullis's Wolves: fast, direct, physical football built on intense preparation and discipline. League champions in 1954, 1958 and 1959.

name: Austria 1931–34 (Wunderteam)
description: Austria's Wunderteam: short passing and position swapping, with a withdrawn centre-forward.

name: Arsenal 1925–34
description: Herbert Chapman's Arsenal: a third back, the stopper, deep defending and counter-attacks. League champions in 1931 and 1933.

name: Hungary 1950–56 (Golden Team)
description: The Golden Team: a withdrawn centre-forward (Hidegkuti), mobile midfielders and first-time passing. Unbeaten from June 1950 to the 1954 World Cup final.

name: River Plate 1941–47 (La Máquina)
description: River Plate's La Máquina: forwards who swap positions, short passing and dribbling. The style that came to define Argentine football.

name: Queen's Park 1872–89
description: Queen's Park of Glasgow: combination play, short passing from player to player in a 2-2-6 shape. The root of the Scottish passing game.
